items.name: button
items.title: Button
items.description: Solid, secondary, outline, ghost, link and destructive buttons with a loading state and asChild for links.
items.docs: Use asChild to render the styles on a Next Link. loading disables the button and shows a spinner.

items.name: badge
items.title: Badge
items.description: Status and metadata labels with success, warning, destructive, outline and muted tones.
items.docs: Status badges carry text as well as colour; never rely on the tone alone.

items.name: skeleton
items.title: Skeleton
items.description: A loading placeholder in the shape of the content, with a shimmer sweep instead of a pulse. Give siblings a delay so the sweep runs as one wave.
items.docs: Match the real layout: a skeleton that does not hold the final shape shifts the page when the data arrives.

items.name: separator
items.title: Separator
items.description: A hairline rule, horizontal or vertical, decorative by default.

items.name: kbd
items.title: Kbd
items.description: A keyboard key for shortcut hints, with a group for combinations.

items.name: input
items.title: Input
items.description: A text input with focus ring, invalid state and file input styling.
items.docs: Pair with Label via htmlFor. Set aria-invalid from your form library to show the error state. fieldSurface is the same surface for Textarea and the Select and Combobox triggers.

items.name: label
items.title: Label
items.description: A form label that focuses its control on click.

items.name: tooltip
items.title: Tooltip
items.description: A tooltip on hover and focus, with a shared provider so a row of controls feels like one surface.
items.docs: Wrap your app once in TooltipProvider. A tooltip is never the only place a label lives.

items.name: dialog
items.title: Dialog
items.description: A modal dialog with focus trap, Escape and backdrop close, and a required title and description.
items.docs: Every DialogContent needs a DialogTitle; hide it visually with sr-only if the design has no heading.

items.name: sheet
items.title: Sheet
items.description: A panel that slides in from any edge: menus, carts, filters. Same accessibility contract as Dialog.
items.docs: Pass side left, right, top or bottom. Sheets slide on transform only.

items.name: tabs
items.title: Tabs
items.description: Tabs with arrow-key navigation, as an underline (line) or a segmented control (pill).
items.docs: Give TabsList the group/list class so the triggers pick up the variant.

items.name: command
items.title: Command
items.description: A filtered, keyboard-driven list on cmdk, inline or as a palette in CommandDialog.
items.docs: CommandDialog brings its own Command root: put CommandInput and CommandList straight inside. It carries a hidden title and description for screen readers.

items.name: rhs-ui-theme
items.title: RHS UI theme
items.description: The RHS UI colour theme: a violet brand ramp on a constant OKLCH hue and a violet-tinted neutral scale, measured for WCAG AA in light and dark. Drops into any shadcn project as the semantic tokens.
items.docs: Installs the RHS semantic tokens into your globals.css. Your components keep their names (bg-background, text-primary); only the values change.

items.title: Select

items.name: select-demo
items.title: select demo
items.description: Interactive preview of the select component.

items.name: combobox
items.title: Combobox
items.description: A field that opens a searchable list, for choices too long to scan: countries, time zones, customers.

items.name: combobox-demo
items.title: combobox demo

items.name: textarea

items.name: textarea-demo
items.title: textarea demo

items.name: popover
items.title: Popover

items.name: popover-demo

items.name: dropdown-menu

items.name: navigation-menu

items.name: navigation-menu-demo

items.name: alert

items.name: alert-dialog-demo

items.name: button-group
items.title: Button group
items.description: Related actions joined into one bar with shared borders and one radius, in a row or a column, stacking on a phone, so a set of buttons reads as a single control.
items.docs: Give the group an aria-label. variant and size reach every button in it (Button, Copy, Async, Download, Upload and the rest) unless that button sets its own. A child with size="icon" takes the square size of the group, and stackBelow turns a long row into a column on a phone. For choosing a value use Toggle Group or Segmented Control.

items.name: split-button
items.title: Split button
items.description: A main action with a chevron that opens the alternatives, like Save and Save as draft: one click does the common thing, the menu holds the rest, and it can remember the choice.
items.docs: The chevron is named "More options for <label>". Loading and disabled apply to the main button only; a loading button is aria-disabled, not disabled, so keyboard focus stays on it. With remember, store the id from onRememberChange and pass it back as rememberedId on the next visit.

items.name: icon-button
items.title: Icon button
items.description: A button that is only an icon but can never be unlabelled: the label is required, shows as a tooltip with its shortcut, and the touch target stays 44px.
items.docs: label is required: it is the accessible name and the tooltip. shortcut only displays keys in the tooltip; bind the key with Shortcut button or your own handler. The badge can appear and disappear while the button has focus, and its count joins the accessible name. Wrap a toolbar in IconButtonProvider so the tooltips share one delay: after the first, the neighbours open at once. tooltip takes over the tooltip's open state.

items.name: icon-button-demo

items.name: copy-button
items.title: Copy button
items.description: A button that copies text and says so: the icon draws into a check, the label becomes Copied, a screen reader hears it, then it resets. It copes with a blocked clipboard.
items.docs: Pass a function as value for text worked out when the button is pressed; it may be async. Where the browser blocks the clipboard the text is selected and the button says to press Ctrl C. status shows a state without pressing.

items.name: copy-button-demo
items.title: Copy button demo

items.name: async-button
items.title: Async button
items.description: A button for an action that takes a moment: it locks while pending, shows success or failure in place without changing width, and returns to rest by itself.
items.docs: Return a promise from onClick, or drive the button from your own state with status={mutation.status}. It uses aria-disabled while pending so focus stays on the button, and it is as wide as its longest label so nothing jumps.

items.name: async-button-demo
items.title: Async button demo
items.description: A working preview of Async button.

items.name: download-button
items.title: Download button
items.description: A download action that tells you what you get: file name, type and size on the button, and a preparing state for files made on demand.
items.docs: Give href for a file that exists (a real link; a cross-origin file may be opened instead of saved) or onDownload for one built when asked. Pass bytes as soon as you know the size; it can arrive after the first render. The accessible name follows the state and always holds the words drawn on the button.

items.name: download-button-demo
items.title: Download button demo
items.description: A working preview of Download button.

items.name: upload-button
items.title: Upload button
items.description: A button that opens the file chooser, also takes drops and pastes, and hands you validated files, with progress on the button itself and a cancel while it uploads.
items.docs: You run the upload: pass state and progress back in. onFiles gets the accepted files and the rejected ones, each with a code and a reason in words (labels.accept replaces the words for what is accepted); show those wherever suits you, or hand the list to File Dropzone.

items.name: upload-button-demo
items.title: Upload button demo
items.description: A working preview of Upload button.

items.name: print-button
items.title: Print button
items.description: Prints one part of the page instead of the whole thing: it hides everything else for the print job and puts the page back afterwards.
items.docs: Pass target as a ref or a selector. Mark anything that must stay off the paper with data-print-hide. The print styles are injected for the length of the job and removed on afterprint.

items.name: print-button-demo
items.title: Print button demo
items.description: A working preview of Print button.

items.name: back-button
items.title: Back button
items.description: A back link that returns to where the person came from and falls back to a safe page when there is no history, so it never leaves your site.
items.docs: It is a real link to fallbackHref. Pass onBack to hand the press to your router: it gets true when the previous page is on your site and false when it is not.

items.name: back-button-demo
items.title: Back button demo
items.description: A working preview of Back button.

items.name: fullscreen-button
items.title: Fullscreen button
items.description: A toggle for fullscreen on any element: icon and label follow the real state, Escape works as the browser makes it, and it hides where unsupported.
items.docs: Mark the element with data-fullscreen-root or pass target, and keep the button inside it. iPhone Safari cannot expand an element: pass fallback to cover the viewport instead, or the button renders nothing there. With words on it the name is the visible label; the icon-only button keeps one name and uses aria-pressed.

items.name: fullscreen-button-demo
items.title: Fullscreen button demo
items.description: A working preview of Fullscreen button.

items.name: shortcut-button
items.title: Shortcut button
items.description: A button that shows its keyboard shortcut and listens for it: the right modifier per platform, ignored while typing, exposed to assistive tech.
items.docs: mod is Cmd on a Mac and Ctrl elsewhere. Sequences like "g i" time out after a second. The shortcut is ignored in text fields unless allowInInputs is set.

items.name: shortcut-button-demo
items.title: Shortcut button demo
items.description: A working preview of Shortcut button.

items.name: undo-redo-buttons
items.title: Undo and redo buttons
items.description: The undo and redo pair of any editor: dimmed when there is nothing to step through, the next step named in the tooltip, and the shortcuts bound for you.
items.docs: You own the history: keep it in a reducer or your editor and wire onUndo and onRedo. Pass the next step as undoLabel ("Undo: Move layer"); it becomes the tooltip and what a screen reader hears afterwards. The keys are ignored inside fields; pass scope to listen only inside an editor.

items.name: undo-redo-buttons-demo
items.title: Undo and redo buttons demo
items.description: A working preview of Undo and redo buttons.

items.name: zoom-controls
items.title: Zoom controls
items.description: Zoom out, the current level, zoom in and fit: one compact control for images, maps, documents and canvases, with keyboard shortcuts and limits.
items.docs: value is a scale (1 is 100 percent); presets are in percent. The keys work while focus is inside the parent of the controls, or inside scope, so the browser's own zoom keeps working elsewhere. onFit adds Fit to screen: you know the content size, so you work out the scale.

items.name: zoom-controls-demo
items.title: Zoom controls demo
items.description: A working preview of Zoom controls.

items.name: record-navigator
items.title: Record navigator
items.description: Previous and next through a queue of records, with the position in words, keyboard shortcuts and the reason a button is off at either end.
items.docs: index counts from zero. Leave total out while a list is loading and the text reads "3 of many". With loop the buttons stay on at the ends and you wrap the index yourself. J and K are ignored while typing. For pages of rows use Pagination.

items.name: record-navigator-demo
items.title: Record navigator demo
items.description: A working preview of Record navigator.

items.name: floating-action-button
items.title: Floating action button
items.description: The round primary action pinned to a corner: it extends to show its label, shrinks to the icon on scroll, and clears the bottom bar and safe area.
items.docs: It is fixed to the viewport; pass className="absolute" to pin it inside a positioned container. Give scrollTarget the ref of the element that scrolls when the page does not. offset lifts it over a bottom navigation, and visible hides it while a dialog is open. With href, disabled dims the link, takes it out of the tab order and stops the navigation.

items.name: floating-action-button-demo
items.title: Floating action button demo
items.description: A working preview of Floating action button.

items.name: speed-dial
items.title: Speed dial
items.description: A floating action that fans out three to five related actions on press, each labelled, reachable by keyboard and closing on Escape or an outside tap.
items.docs: The first action is the one nearest the trigger. Arrow keys move, Home and End jump, typing a letter finds an action, Escape closes. Like the floating action button it is fixed to the viewport; pass className="absolute" to keep it inside a container. direction="left" hangs each label above its button, so it needs short labels, and three actions take about 260px of width: on a phone use two or three.

items.name: speed-dial-demo
items.title: Speed dial demo
items.description: A working preview of Speed dial.

items.name: overflow-actions
items.title: Overflow actions
items.description: A row of actions that moves whatever does not fit into a More menu, by priority, measured on resize, so a toolbar works at every width.
items.docs: Give it the width of its container (it is a block, w-full). pinned actions never move; a lower priority leaves first. Use separatorBefore to keep groups in the menu, and onOverflowChange to learn which ids moved.

items.name: overflow-actions-demo
items.title: Overflow actions demo
items.description: A working preview of Overflow actions.

items.name: hold-to-confirm-button
items.title: Hold to confirm button
items.description: A destructive action you have to hold to trigger: a fill runs across the button, releasing early cancels, and a keyboard and screen reader path exists.
items.docs: onConfirm runs once. A quick press is the other way in: it says "Press again to confirm" and a second press within three seconds confirms. Keep label honest about the gesture ("Hold to delete project"); the button is as wide as its longest state.

items.name: hold-to-confirm-button-demo
items.title: Hold to confirm button demo
items.description: A working preview of Hold to confirm button.

items.name: resend-button
items.title: Resend button
items.description: A Resend code button with a cooldown: a live countdown while waiting, sending and sent states, and an attempt limit that says what to do next.
items.docs: onResend returns a promise; a rejection shows its message and does not start the timer. maxAttempts counts resends made with this button, and startCooling begins in the waiting state right after the first send. The countdown is announced only at the start, at 10 seconds and at 0, and the button's name stays "Resend code" (labels.ready) while it waits, so a screen reader is not told the time every second.

items.name: resend-button-demo
items.title: Resend button demo
items.description: A working preview of Resend button.

items.name: heading-anchor-link
items.title: Heading anchor link
items.description: The # beside a heading that lets a section be linked to: it copies the URL with the fragment, says so, and works from the keyboard.
items.docs: The id goes on the heading; without one no link is drawn. offset is the height of a sticky header, as scroll-margin-top. The link is a sibling of the heading, so the heading's own name stays clean for screen readers, and it is named after its heading (label takes {heading}), so a list of links tells them apart.

items.name: heading-anchor-link-demo
items.title: Heading anchor link demo
items.description: A working preview of Heading anchor link.

items.name: paste-button
items.title: Paste button
items.description: Paste from the clipboard with one press: it asks permission, checks the text, and says what it pasted, why it refused, or how to allow access.
items.docs: The clipboard is read only when the button is pressed. Pass targetRef to fill and focus an input, and validate to refuse text with a reason. Where the browser blocks or lacks readText it focuses the field and says to press Ctrl V; pass read for a native shell.

items.name: paste-button-demo
items.title: Paste button demo
items.description: A working preview of Paste button.

items.name: autoplay-toggle
items.title: Autoplay toggle
items.description: The pause control moving content must have: one button to stop and start a carousel, ticker or video, with a hook that also holds it on hover, focus and hidden tabs.
items.docs: label says what it controls and is part of the name (Pause testimonials, Play testimonials). Let useAutoplay own the state, spread contentProps on the moving content and read running in the timer; there is no aria-pressed because the name already follows the state.

items.name: autoplay-toggle-demo
items.title: Autoplay toggle demo
items.description: A working preview of Autoplay toggle.

items.name: insert-between-button
items.title: Insert between button
items.description: The plus that appears between two items so you can insert one right there: on hover and focus, always on touch, and reachable by keyboard.
items.docs: index is the position the new item takes; the name reads Insert step between 2 and 3 (pass between for real names). Put one in every gap of your list, and move focus to the new item in onInsert.

items.name: insert-between-button-demo
items.title: Insert between button demo
items.description: A working preview of Insert between button.

items.name: swap-button
items.title: Swap button
items.description: Swap two values with one press, like origin and destination or from and to: the icon turns, both fields trade places, and it says what changed.
items.docs: Give it labelA, labelB and the current values so it can say what changed. With seam it centres on its parent, which must be relative, and reaches (size minus gap) / 2 into each field: leave a 20px gap between fields padded 16px (gap-5) so it clears their text and its focus ring has room. swapValues(state, 'from', 'to') is a pure helper for the common two-field state.

items.name: swap-button-demo
items.title: Swap button demo
items.description: A working preview of Swap button.

items.name: status-badge
items.title: Status badge
items.description: A badge for a record's state with a glyph and a word, so draft, paid, overdue and archived read without colour.
items.docs: Pass any string as status; known keys get their glyph and emphasis, others get a neutral outline. Extend the vocabulary with statuses, spreading defaultStatuses. The text is the status; the dot size keeps an sr-only label.

items.name: status-badge-demo
items.title: Status badge demo
items.description: A working preview of Status badge.

items.name: chip
items.title: Chip
items.description: A compact pill that is static, selectable or removable, with an icon or avatar: the unit behind filters, picks and attributes.
items.docs: toggle chips are buttons with aria-pressed and a check. An input chip's remove button is named Remove <label>; Backspace or Delete on it removes the chip and focus moves to its neighbour. Pass removeLabel when the label is not plain text.

items.name: chip-demo
items.title: Chip demo
items.description: A working preview of Chip.

items.name: tag-list
items.title: Tag list
items.description: A row of tags that never breaks the layout: it shows what fits, then a '+3' button that opens the rest.
items.docs: Give the list a width to fit into (a table column or max-w class), then fit shows what fits and max caps the count; before it has measured, the server HTML shows only the whole tags that fit one line. The group is named like Design, Research and 3 more. Tags with an href are links; others call onTagSelect.

items.name: tag-list-demo
items.title: Tag list demo
items.description: A working preview of Tag list.

items.name: formatted-number
items.title: Formatted number
items.description: Numbers formatted for the reader: compact (1.2K), percent, unit or currency, in tabular figures with the full value kept for assistive technology.
items.docs: The Intl style option is called format here, because style belongs to CSS. percent takes a fraction (0.12 is 12%); currency needs currency and unit needs unit, which the types enforce, and if Intl still refuses a code it writes a plain decimal with the code. Compact figures keep the full number in the accessible name and a tooltip that opens on hover and on a tap; add focusable for a keyboard tab stop. null and NaN show the placeholder.

items.name: formatted-number-demo
items.title: Formatted number demo
items.description: A working preview of Formatted number.

items.name: money-amount
items.title: Money amount
items.description: An amount of money with currency, sign and meaning in words, for credits, debits and refunds, in tabular figures.
items.docs: amount is an integer in minor units (1250 is 12.50; JPY has none); a fraction is rounded to the nearest minor unit. direction credit, debit, refund or auto (the sign of the amount) decides the sign, the weight and the sr-only word. A currency code Intl rejects is written as digits and the code. Meaning never depends on red and green.

items.name: money-amount-demo
items.title: Money amount demo
items.description: A working preview of Money amount.

items.name: link-card
items.title: Link card
items.description: A card that is one link: icon or image, title, description and an arrow, with a focus ring around the whole card.
items.docs: The title is the only link, stretched over the card. With asChild, pass your framework link as the child (a Next Link with no text and its own href); the title is added inside it. external adds an arrow and a hidden opens in a new tab.

items.name: link-card-demo
items.title: Link card demo
items.description: A working preview of Link card.

items.name: due-date-label
items.title: Due date label
items.description: A due date in words that matter: 'Due today', 'Due in 3 days' or 'Overdue by 2 days', with an icon that carries the urgency.
items.docs: Days are compared as calendar days in timeZone, so a task due today never reads overdue at 00:01. A date-only string like 2026-10-24 is a calendar date and never shifts. The full date is in a tooltip that opens on hover and on a tap; add focusable for a keyboard tab stop, or showDate to write it into the line (Due in 3 days · Fri 23 Oct) for phones and print. Pass now for tests; otherwise it reads the browser clock after hydration.

items.name: due-date-label-demo
items.title: Due date label demo
items.description: A working preview of Due date label.

items.name: inline-code
items.title: Inline code
items.description: Code inside a sentence: a quiet mono chip that wraps cleanly, with an optional click to copy.
items.docs: It inherits the surrounding font size. copyable turns the chip into a Copy button; pass value when the children are not plain text. Your other props land on the code, or on the button when it is copyable. Plain inline code is a Server Component; only the copyable part is a client module.

items.name: inline-code-demo
items.title: Inline code demo
items.description: A working preview of Inline code.

items.name: icons
items.title: Icons
items.description: The RHS UI icon set: one drawing hand for every glyph, a 1.75px stroke on a 24 grid with the open corner as its signature. Sized by size, coloured by currentColor, with Glyph to draw your own.
items.docs: Import the glyphs you need from "@rhs-ui/icons". Pass a title when an icon is the only label. Draw your own glyph in the same hand with <Glyph d="..." />.

items.name: animated-icon
items.title: Animated icon
items.description: The engine behind the animated icons: hover, focus, loop and first-view triggers through the Web Animations API, a two-state frame in plain CSS, and reduced motion respected. No animation library.
items.docs: Installed with every animated icon. Motion icons take trigger: hover (default, follows the button or link around the icon), loop, appear or static. State icons take active.

items.name: animated-icon-demo
items.title: Animated icon demo
items.description: Animated icons in buttons: a bell on hover, a refresh that loops while syncing, and a copy icon that turns into a check.

items.name: animated-bell
items.title: Animated bell
items.description: A bell that rings: the body swings from its crown and the clapper follows a beat later. For notifications and reminders.
items.docs: Inside a Button it rings when the button is hovered or focused. Use trigger="loop" while there are unread notifications.

items.name: animated-search
items.title: Animated search
items.description: A lens that looks left and right before it settles. For search, filter and lookup actions.
items.docs: Use trigger="loop" while results are loading.

items.name: animated-arrow-right
items.title: Animated arrow right
items.description: An arrow that leaves on the right and comes back in from the left. For continue, next and call-to-action buttons.
items.docs: Place it after the label: <Button>Continue <IconArrowRightAnimated /></Button>.

items.name: animated-heart
items.title: Animated heart
items.description: A heart that beats twice, the second beat softer than the first. For favourites, wishlists and likes.

meta.usage:
<Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label="Save to wishlist" aria-pressed={saved}>
  <IconHeartAnimated />
</Button>

items.docs: Pair it with aria-pressed on the wishlist button; the icon only shows the gesture.

items.name: animated-sparkle
items.title: Animated sparkle
items.description: A four-point star that turns a quarter and lands on itself while the small star pops back in. For new, highlight and AI states.
items.docs: Use trigger="loop" sparingly: one moving sparkle on a page is a highlight, three is noise.

items.name: animated-refresh
items.title: Animated refresh
items.description: One eased full turn on hover, or a steady loop while something syncs.
items.docs: Switch to trigger="loop" while syncing and set aria-busy on the button; it finishes its turn when you switch back.

items.name: animated-download
items.title: Animated download
items.description: The arrow drops through the tray and comes back from the top while the tray gives a little. For download and export actions.
items.docs: Inside a download link it plays on hover and on keyboard focus of the link.

items.name: animated-trash
items.title: Animated trash
items.description: The lid lifts from its left hinge and drops shut. For delete and remove actions.
items.docs: An icon-only delete button still needs an accessible label: <Button size="icon" aria-label="Delete">.

items.name: animated-send
items.title: Animated send
items.description: A paper plane that flies off to the top right and glides back in from the bottom left. For send, share and submit.
items.docs: Plays on hover and focus of the submit button it sits in.

items.name: animated-cart
items.title: Animated cart
items.description: A product drops into the basket and the cart dips under its weight. For add-to-cart buttons and cart links.
items.docs: At rest it is the cart glyph; the product only shows while it moves.

items.name: animated-check-circle
items.title: Animated check circle
items.description: The ring draws itself and then the check. For success states, best with trigger appear.

meta.usage: Your order is confirmed.

items.docs: <IconCheckCircleAnimated trigger="appear" /> draws once when a confirmation scrolls into view.

items.name: animated-copy
items.title: Animated copy
items.description: A copy icon that turns into a drawn check while active. For confirming a copy to the clipboard.
items.docs: Set active for a moment after navigator.clipboard.writeText resolves, and announce it in a live region.

items.name: animated-menu
items.title: Animated menu
items.description: Three lines that fold into a cross while active. For the open state of a navigation menu.

meta.usage:
<Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label="Menu" aria-expanded={open} onClick={toggle}>
  <IconMenuAnimated active={open} />
</Button>

items.docs: Bind active to the menu's open state and aria-expanded on the button.

items.name: animated-sun-moon
items.title: Animated sun and moon
items.description: The sun draws in its rays and turns into the moon while active. For a light and dark theme switch.

meta.usage:
<Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label="Dark theme" aria-pressed={dark} onClick={toggleTheme}>
  <IconSunMoonAnimated active={dark} />
</Button>

items.docs: Bind active to the resolved theme after hydration, so the server and the first client render agree.

items.name: animated-settings
items.title: Animated settings
items.description: A gear that turns one tooth and settles while the hub gives a little. For settings and preferences.
items.docs: Inside a settings button it turns on hover and on keyboard focus. Use trigger="loop" while preferences are saving.

items.name: animated-mail
items.title: Animated mail
items.description: The flap folds open and a letter rises out before everything closes again. For mail, invites and messages.
items.docs: Use it in a contact or invite action; trigger="appear" plays it once when the section scrolls into view.

items.name: animated-upload
items.title: Animated upload
items.description: The arrow leaves through the top and comes back from the tray, which gives under it. For upload and import actions.
items.docs: Switch to trigger="loop" while a file is uploading and set aria-busy on the button.

items.name: animated-star
items.title: Animated star
items.description: A fifth of a turn lands the star back on itself, with a pop at the end. For ratings, favourites and highlights.

meta.usage:
<Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label="Add to favourites" aria-pressed={starred}>
  <IconStarAnimated />
</Button>

items.docs: Pair it with aria-pressed on a favourite button; the icon shows the gesture, the button holds the state.

items.name: animated-log-out

items.name: animated-phone
items.title: Animated phone

items.name: animated-clock
items.title: Animated clock

items.name: animated-message
items.title: Animated message

items.name: animated-lock
items.title: Animated lock

items.docs: Set active when whatever it guards is unlocked, and mirror that in the button label or aria-pressed.

items.name: animated-eye
items.title: Animated eye
items.description: The eye closes behind a line that draws itself. For showing and hiding a password or a value.

meta.usage:
<Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label={shown ? "Hide password" : "Show password"} onClick={toggle}>
  <IconEyeAnimated active={shown} />
</Button>

items.docs: Set active when the content is hidden; the button label should change with it (Show password, Hide password).

items.name: animated-play-pause

items.name: animated-plus
items.title: Animated plus

items.name: animated-bookmark

items.docs: Page asks for a reason first and waits for `onPage` to settle; reject the promise to show the failure and keep the reason. With no `current` shift the card says Nobody is on call and offers to page the escalation contact. Pass `now` for a stable first render.

items.docs: Counts are yours to compute: pass how many rows each option would leave given the other filters. Options at zero stay in place, dimmed, so the list never reshuffles while people click. The button's accessible name lists the picks, and on a narrow screen long names in the chips give way with an ellipsis. The list is a multi-select checklist named after the filter, and each option says whether it is checked. Controlled with `value` and `onValueChange`, or uncontrolled with `defaultValue`.

items.description: The row of controls above a list: search, your filters and a Reset that counts what is active, folding into one Filters button and a sheet on a phone.
items.docs: Your filters are rendered once and moved between the row and the sheet, so they keep their state, an open panel included. Server rendered, the markup already has the phone's shape at the default 640px (CSS decides until the page is interactive); another `collapseBelow` applies once it is. Reset calls `onReset`, and clearing your filters is yours to do; Done only closes the sheet. Keep the filters controlled so a page reload can restore them. A facet filter's button sizes to its picks, so the controls after it make room when they change.

items.name: dashboard-grid
items.title: Dashboard grid
items.description: A 12-column grid for dashboard widgets: sizes by name, rows of one fixed height so tall and short widgets line up, and one column on a phone.
items.docs: It lays out and nothing else, and it needs no client code. Breakpoints follow the grid's own width (container queries), so it adapts beside a sidebar: twelve columns from 896px, six from 672px, one below. Give every Widget a `label`: each becomes a region. A widget's only child fills it. Row spans apply from the tablet layout up; on a phone a widget is as tall as its content. With `dense` the visual order can differ from the DOM order.

items.docs: The panel is not in the page until it is opened, so it costs nothing on a table with fifty metrics. Pass `refreshedAt` and, when a source is stale after a different time, `staleAfterHours`. `now` is only for demos and tests. Long names, formulas and table names wrap inside the panel. Focus lands on the panel; Tab then reaches the close button, the copy button and the owner link.

items.name: reveal
items.title: Reveal
items.description: Brings an element forward as it scrolls into view, tied to the scroll: rise, tilt, scale, blur or slide.
items.docs: Pure CSS scroll-driven animation: nothing is hidden before hydration, and reduced motion or a browser without scroll timelines shows the element at rest. Give a row of reveals an increasing order to land them in sequence. Clip a parent with overflow: clip, never overflow: hidden: a hidden overflow makes that parent the scroll container the timeline follows, and the animation stands still.

items.docs: Put layers with different speeds in one relatively positioned section. Keep speeds between -0.6 and 0.6 for text, and use the stronger values for shapes and images. items.name: top-loading-bar
items.title: Top loading bar
items.description: A thin bar across the top that races to 80 percent while a page or action is pending, then sweeps to the end and fades. Work shorter than a delay never shows it.
items.docs: Pass active from a router transition, a form action or a pending flag; mount one bar near the top of the layout. It is fixed to the viewport by default: give it className="absolute" inside a relatively positioned panel. The bar waits delay milliseconds (150 by default) before it shows, so fast work never flashes it, and it is announced once as a polite status with the label you give it. Under reduced motion it is a still line that appears and disappears. Switch tone to destructive just before a failing run ends.

items.name: count-up
items.title: Count up
items.description: A number that counts up from zero the first time it is mostly on screen, with prefix, suffix, decimals and locale, and the final value in the page from the start.
items.docs: The final value is in the page from the first render, in text for screen readers, search engines and print; the visible digits sit in a box as wide as that value, so nothing shifts while they run. It counts when 40 percent of the number is on screen. A number that is already on screen when the page hydrates keeps its final value, one that mounts in the browser always counts. Reduced motion and browsers without IntersectionObserver show the final value at once. Pass your application locale.

items.name: fill-bar
items.title: Fill bar
items.description: A labelled bar that fills to its value when it scrolls into view, for skills, quotas and survey results, built on Progress so the real value is always in the page.
items.docs: It renders the Progress primitive, so the progressbar role, its name and the true value are present from the first render and only the drawing animates. Give bars in a group an increasing order to land them in sequence. format is percent, value or fraction; pass valueText for anything else ("7.2 of 10 GB"). Use tone="muted" for the rows that are not the point and tone="destructive" for a limit that has been hit, and say so in the value text too. A value past max draws a full bar and one below zero an empty bar, while the text still shows the real number. Reduced motion, and a bar already on screen when the page hydrates, show the final width at once.

items.name: fade-in
items.title: Fade in
items.description: A wrapper that fades and lifts its content in once when it enters view, with direction, delay and duration. Visible without JavaScript and under reduced motion.
items.docs: Reveal is tied to the scroll position; FadeIn plays on its own clock, which suits cards and copy the reader will not scrub. The server renders the block fully visible, so nothing is hidden without JavaScript or before hydration. A block that is already on screen when the page hydrates stays as it is; one that mounts in the browser, such as a route change or a conditional, always plays. Use delay to line a row of blocks up. Only opacity and transform move, so layout never shifts, and reduced motion and print show everything at rest.

items.name: stagger-list
items.title: Stagger list
items.description: A list whose items enter one after another when it scrolls into view, with a step, a cap on the wait and real list semantics that stay intact.
items.docs: Render it as ul or ol and give it li children; it adds no wrapper, and a ul or ol carries an explicit role="list", so assistive technology (Safari with VoiceOver included) still announces the list and its item count. Each child waits index times step milliseconds, never longer than maxDelay. Any element can be an item. The server renders every item visible; a list already on screen when the page hydrates stays as it is, one that mounts in the browser always plays. Reduced motion and print show every item at once.

items.name: crossfade
items.title: Crossfade
items.description: Swap content with a soft crossfade and no layout jump: tab panels, loaded states and changing values, with the leaving content made inert.
items.docs: Render the content for the current key as children and change activeKey when it changes; the previous content stays mounted just long enough to fade out. Old and new share one grid cell, so during the fade the box is as tall as the taller of the two. When the heights differ, wrap Crossfade in AutoHeight so the rest of the page glides to the new height instead of snapping once the fade ends. The leaving content is inert and hidden from assistive technology the moment it starts leaving. Pass moveFocus to move focus to the new content after a change. mode="wait" lets the old content leave before the new arrives. Reduced motion swaps instantly.

items.name: auto-height
items.title: Auto height
items.description: A container that glides to its new height when its content changes, for form steps, inline errors and swapped panels, without ever clipping a focus ring.
items.docs: Wrap the part of a layout whose height changes. A ResizeObserver watches the content, so it follows your own state, images that load and text that wraps. Height is pinned only while it moves; afterwards it is auto again and overflow is released, so focus rings and shadows are never clipped. Give it aria-live="polite" when what appears is a message (an inline error), and keep the element mounted so the region exists before its content does. Reduced motion applies the change at once; pass disabled to turn the glide off.

items.name: sticky-section-header
items.title: Sticky section header
items.description: Section headings that stick under the page header while their section scrolls, with a hairline and solid background only when stuck.
items.docs: Put one header at the top of each section, as a direct child of the section: it sticks while its section is in view and the next one pushes it away. It is native position: sticky, so Page Down, find in page and screen magnifiers behave. Set offset to the height of a fixed navbar above. Sticking needs no overflow: hidden between the header and its scroll area; use overflow: clip instead. Give the scroll area a scroll-padding-top equal to the header height so focused items are never hidden behind it.

items.name: scroll-focus-list
items.title: Scroll focus list
items.description: A list where the item at the reading line is at full strength and the rest step back, for steps, features and long lists, always at readable contrast.
items.docs: It watches a thin band at lineAt (0.45 by default) with an IntersectionObserver, in the nearest scrolling box or the page, so there is no scroll listener. The row at the line gets aria-current and data-active; render lets you draw your own rows and read that state. Other rows step back only as far as your muted-foreground, never lighter, so contrast stays at AA, and the description of the current row steps up toward your foreground; dim sets how far. Space the rows with the --rhs-focus-gap variable, and leave room above the first and below the last so each can reach the line. Under reduced motion the other rows are not dimmed, and without JavaScript nothing is.

items.name: edge-fade-scroller
items.title: Edge fade scroller
items.description: A scroll container that fades its edges only where there is more to scroll, for chip rows, menus and long lists, and never covers text.
items.docs: The fade is a CSS mask, so it works on any background and never covers text or catches a click. Its width follows the scroll position, so it grows as you leave an edge and is gone when nothing overflows. Scrolling stays native: keyboard, wheel and touch are untouched, and an item focused with the keyboard scrolls to a spot clear of the fade. When nothing inside is focusable, pass label to make the box a labelled region you can scroll with the keyboard; its focus ring is drawn outside the fade. onReachEnd fires once each time the end is reached, for loading the next page. Give a horizontal row a flex layout through className.

items.name: drag-scroll
items.title: Drag scroll
items.description: A horizontal strip you can drag with a mouse, with optional snap and edge arrows, and full keyboard support. Touch keeps its native scroll.
items.docs: Mouse and pen drag the strip with a short glide when released; a drag never clicks the item under it. Touch keeps native scrolling. The strip is a focusable region named by label: arrow keys move by an item, Home and End jump to the ends. The wheel moves it sideways only while the pointer is over it, no modifier is held and there is room that way, so the page is never trapped. snap settles on the start or centre of an item. arrows adds previous and next buttons, shown only on devices with a fine pointer and only where there is more to scroll. className styles the wrapper; other props go to the strip.

items.name: scroll-aware-header
items.title: Scroll aware header
items.description: A sticky header that hides on the way down and returns on the way up, or condenses, or turns solid, without trapping focus or shifting the page.
items.docs: Make it a direct child of the page or scroll area it should stick in. behavior="hide" slides away while scrolling down and returns on scroll up; condense shrinks its padding and gains a hairline; solid turns from transparent to solid. It never hides at the top, while anything inside it has focus, or while a menu in it is open (an element with aria-expanded="true"). Tabbing into a hidden header brings it back. Only transform animates for hide, and condensing trades padding for margin so the page below never moves. Set the padding with --rhs-header-py and --rhs-header-py-condensed. Scroll handling is passive and runs once per frame; reduced motion toggles instantly.

items.name: reading-time-left
items.title: Reading time left
items.description: A reading-time readout that counts down as you read an article, from its real word count, ending in a quiet Done. Screen readers hear the total once and are never interrupted.
items.docs: Point target at the article with a ref or a CSS selector: its words are counted and the reader's position through it drives the readout. It shows the total at the top ("3 min read"), counts the minutes left, and ends on Done. It redraws at most once a second and is never announced; a screen reader gets the total once. It renders no text on the server. It pairs with Scroll progress rather than replacing it. Translate it with labels (use {minutes} for the number) or take over completely with format.

items.name: scroll-away
items.title: Scroll away
items.description: The exit counterpart to Reveal: hero text and headers fade, lift and soften as they scroll off the top, in pure CSS with no scroll handler.
items.docs: Pure CSS on a view timeline: nothing is hidden before hydration, and reduced motion or a browser without scroll timelines leaves the content fully visible. It ends invisible and, once it has, ignores the pointer, so a link you can still see always works and one that has gone cannot be pressed. Pair it with Reveal (Reveal outside, ScrollAway inside) for something that arrives and leaves with the scroll. It owns opacity, transform and filter while it runs; put your own on a child. Clip a parent with overflow: clip, never overflow: hidden: a hidden overflow makes that parent the scroll container the timeline follows, and the animation stands still.

items.name: render-on-view
items.title: Render on view
items.description: Mounts heavy content such as a map, a chart or an embed only when it nears the viewport, holding its space so nothing shifts.
items.docs: Give it the height the content will have, as minHeight or ratio, so the page does not jump when it arrives. Keep headings, landmarks and anything a crawler must read outside it, and use forceRender for print, bots and tests. With once off the content unmounts again when it is far away and the space it measured is kept. Inside a scrolling panel the margin cannot reach past the panel's own edge, so content there mounts as it enters the panel.

items.name: stick-to-bottom
items.title: Stick to bottom
items.description: A scroll area for chats and logs that follows new content while you are at the end, and offers a Jump to latest button once you scroll up.
items.docs: Give it a height with className (h-80, or h-full inside a flex column). It follows only while the reader is at the end: scroll up and it lets go, and the button counts what arrived (pass newCount to count yourself, for example when you trim old items). Items are announced politely, and only while it follows; while the reader is away, the count of what arrived is announced as a status instead, at most every few seconds. Growth that arrives later, such as an image that loads, is followed too. A stream that updates many times a second reads best with behavior="instant". To pull the reader to the end after they send something, scroll an element at the end of your list into view. Under reduced motion every jump is instant.

items.name: snap-pages
items.title: Snap pages
items.description: Full-height sections that snap into place as you scroll, with a dot rail and keyboard paging, on native CSS scroll snap.
items.docs: One screen tall by default (h-dvh); give it h-full to fill a parent. Give each page its own className for a background, and flex items-center to centre what it holds. Keep the right edge of a page free for the dot rail, around 4rem on a phone. A page taller than the screen scrolls normally and the keys follow it: Page Down moves on only when its end is in view. Reduced motion softens mandatory snapping to proximity and switches off gliding.

items.name: view-video
items.title: View video
items.description: A muted video that plays while it is mostly in view and rests when it is not, with a pause button that is always there and a poster.
items.docs: For loops and product demos with no sound: the video is always muted and inline. Give it a poster that matches the first frame, so playback starts without a jump, and a label that says what the clip shows. Pass sources with WebM first and MP4 as the fallback. It plays at half visible (threshold), rests off screen and in a background tab, and a pause you press sticks until you press play. Under reduced motion it never starts by itself. Only metadata loads until the video is a screen away. onPlayingChange tells you when it starts and stops, for a status label or analytics. The control stays a dark disc with a light glyph in every theme, so it reads over any frame.

items.title: View video demo

items.name: smooth-scroll
items.title: Smooth scroll
items.description: Optional eased, inertial scrolling for the page or one box, on Lenis, that never fights the browser: scrollbar, Page keys and anchors still work.
items.docs: Wrap the app once for page scrolling, or wrap one box with root={false} and give it a height. It eases the wheel only, and turns itself off on touch screens, under reduced motion and when enabled is false; scrollTo then falls back to a plain jump, so a button that calls it never goes dead. It lets go when the scrollbar, Page Down or an anchor takes the scroll mid-ease, pauses while a dialog locks the page, and leaves nested scrollers, menus and dialogs alone; mark any other area with data-lenis-prevent. Do not combine it with CSS scroll-behavior: smooth or scroll snap on the same scroller. Use one page-level provider, and read scrollTo and active with useSmoothScroll.
